# engineering-review-core

These are exact source excerpts, not a claim of whole-document reading. Apply only your assigned role and active workflow. Preloading never expands tools, execution permissions, review layers or file scope.

Record `Rules loaded: <skill names>; <source SHA-256>; <included sections>; missing/changed rules` once in retained invocation evidence. Configured skills alone do not prove delivery: require the injected content in your own context. If missing, read the applicable originals with permitted tools and report the setup gap.

Compare fingerprints with current source evidence supplied by the coordinator. Never run Bash/git merely to validate these rules. Project-specific rules override only their explicit fields.

Included sections satisfy their first-entry reading requirement. All other applicable sections and project design rules, including their exceptions, still require targeted reading. ### Core rules for Claude preload

This is the user-approved operational core, not Nishiguchi's wording or proof of company-wide adoption. Preserve the pinned source and the separate human-review reference. Explicit project rules and platform/user controls retain their precedence. Do not invent quotations or export one project's conventions to another project.

- Responsibility: identify the actual owner/layer and a concrete mixed responsibility before requesting a boundary change. Reuse existing validated concepts, but do not merge contracts merely because their fields match.
- Exceptions: catch for recovery, error translation, cleanup or meaningful context. Preserve unexpected failures and their cause. Do not remove every catch or accept an empty catch.
- Types: validate untrusted boundaries and narrow types. An annotation/cast is not runtime validation; a justified framework assertion is not automatically a defect. Check the actual producer and nearest guard before asserting reachability.
- Intake: before substantive judgment, record injected/read/missing rule sections and applicable project design exceptions once. Read required missing originals; an empty Glob is not absence. Inspect changed responsibilities and necessary surrounding code, expanding with a reason rather than requiring full files by default. User/project whole-file requirements and all pending obligations remain.
- Scope/design: make the smallest design-correct change, including required boundary repair. Read applicable project rules and their exceptions. A sourced mandatory violation needs no invented crash; an optional preference is not a blocker.
- Evidence: separate reachable defects, mandatory-rule violations, verification gaps and optional observations. Record inspected revision/source and the obligation behind the expected behavior. Missing evidence never becomes approval; retain supplied unresolved findings and handoffs until the owning reviewer confirms closure or withdraws with evidence. Never use Info classification to close an unresolved mandatory obligation.
- Ownership: implementation owns edits; each requested review layer retains its own scope. L1.5 stays self-contained. HQ and first-pass L2 must obtain applicable React/Nest consultation after tracing the boundary; implementation advice does not replace independent L2 evidence. Consultants advise only on their assigned boundary, and review-planner routes metadata only. This does not authorize an additional layer or delegate.
- Execution: the active workflow and actual tool restrictions decide execution permissions. In codex-claude-review, all Claude reviewers/consultants stay review-only and Codex owns commands, tests, fixes and CI. A normal Claude session may execute an explicit user request with available permissions. Never bypass restrictions through another agent.
- Completeness: budgets do not waive mandatory rules, consultation, blocker closure or current-snapshot evidence. A clean single-layer result does not grant four-layer/final/merge approval. Read the detailed source index, triggered ASYNC-1/HTTP-1, phase ownership, minor-finding/closure rules and retained-blocker obligations when relevant and not already injected. Preserve their conditions and exceptions.

- Re-review delivery (codex-claude-review only): after full initial review and batch fixes, send the scoped fix delta and planned verification results together once to the same parent/child. Include command/cases/exit/source, limits, and a permitted test/script reference or necessary assertions plus import/load target. Reuse unchanged evidence. Failed, waived, unavailable, not-run or partial checks keep their reasons and pending obligations; they are not success or closure. Evidence-backed earlier questions/user-directed continuations are explicit exceptions. Never require full manifests/logs or weaken read-only and layer boundaries.


### Claude role-scoped intake

For Claude owners, record resolved original paths/versions, complete injected/read sections and missing obligations in the existing `Rules loaded` record. A complete active role definition already injected into your own system prompt needs no self-Read when its correspondence to the current original path/version is verified through invocation/source evidence. The same applies to exact rule sections actually delivered in your own context. A role name, skills declaration, parent's summary or another owner's reading is insufficient. If identity, delivery or retained text is missing, recover only the necessary original clauses, including exceptions; keep dependent approval pending. Do not reread a verified definition merely to confirm your role or format the result.

Use the Claude platform contract. Codex routing/model/implementation instructions in `.codex/AGENTS.md` are not a default Claude-child reading assignment. Resolve a workflow beside that file without loading its full text. Explicit project/common instructions and directly applicable cross-platform clauses still apply; read any such required originals and exceptions. In `codex-claude-review`, the coordinator reads the complete workflow once; reviewers independently read the complete original sections selected by `review_entry.role_sections`, plus any triggered cross-references. Keep the actual path/version and section keys, not a parent-written replacement contract. A narrower delivery never waives permissions, approval conditions, handoffs or the eleven-field result.

Batch independent Read/Glob/Grep requests when their combined results fit the tool and response limits. Plan bounded reads of complete relevant sections; on truncation count only visible complete ranges and recover missing/uncertain ranges with context, not the whole previous document. Reuse your own verified readings throughout the pass and same-owner continuations. Do not create another manifest or duplicate report. All non-injected mandatory rules, design sections and exceptions remain required. Explicit project whole-file requirements still apply, including changed-file reading; reading a test does not transfer QA/E2E adequacy ownership to L2.

### User-directed execution permissions

This is a user-approved operational rule, not a quotation from the human review guidelines.

Autonomous review without an explicit execution request does not start typecheck, lint, build, tests, Playwright, CI or other verification commands.

For `Workflow: codex-claude-review`, Claude and its review subagents only inspect sources and supplied evidence. Codex owns command execution, test creation, CI operations and fixes. A message cannot expand the restricted CLI toolset of an existing review session.

When the user explicitly requests execution in a normal Claude Code session, the main Claude session or an authorized implementation/verification owner may perform those actions with its available permissions. If an existing restricted session cannot execute them, use a separate normal session. Do not treat this direct request as an autonomous review or an automatic Codex-to-Claude review.


## Evidence and reporting

Write user-facing results in polite, plain Japanese. State the decision first and keep sentences short.
`Checked` means inspected file/content. `Executed` means an observed command run; imported CI evidence must identify its source, revision, command/test, and result.
Never invent a test command, execution, line number, requirement, or original quotation. Suggested verification is labeled not executed.
When a rule source is missing, mark the affected judgment unconfirmed, not the rule violated. Do not block unrelated work solely because an optional document is absent.

Final approval requires complete evidence for the requested layer, completed required consultation, and no unresolved blocker affecting that judgment.
A scoped clean result is not full PR approval. A single-layer approval is valid only for that layer and snapshot, is not four-layer or final approval, and joins a later four-layer run only as Supplied evidence. Confirmed open blockers keep overall merge readiness at `REQUEST_CHANGES`; missing blocking evidence keeps it deferred.

For `codex-claude-review` single-layer results, apply the workflow's `single_layer.approval`, `handoff_policy` and `result_consistency`. With complete current-snapshot local coverage, required evidence/consultation, no local findings (including Low), questions or unchecked obligations, and an accepted native verdict, the owner reports `decision: APPROVE` even when independent other-layer handoffs remain open. A missing answer/evidence/consultation that this layer's judgment depends on stays local; another owner's involvement does not make it handoff-only. Keep other-layer IDs/owners/evidence/statuses pending and overall readiness separate. Required handoffs still block final workflow handoff until closed. Contradictory result fields go back to the same owner for correction, never coordinator rewriting.

CR handoffs have no count limit. Keep the existing four fields `Owner/route | Question | Evidence | Required confirmation` and the existing ledger IDs/statuses. Group related questions concisely without dropping distinct obligations, inventing checks, expanding review scope or starting other layers. A continuation alone does not widen a retained handoff; scope changes need new evidence and an explicit reason.

## Responsibility Separation

### Finding
Approval screens contained award-grant logic directly.

### Why It Matters
UI/request flows should not own unrelated domain workflows.
Mixing responsibilities increases review complexity and future maintenance cost.

### Reject Condition
- approval/request UI directly performs award-grant workflow
- unrelated domain workflows mixed into same service/component

### Preferred Pattern
- approval flow delegates to dedicated award service
- workflows separated by domain responsibility


## Exception Handling

### Finding
Unnecessary try/catch blocks existed with empty or meaningless catch logic.

### Why It Matters
Redundant exception handling hides true error boundaries and duplicates global policy.

### Reject Condition
- empty catch
- catch that only rethrows
- catch without recovery, mapping, cleanup, or logging context

### Preferred Pattern
- rely on common exception handling
- add try/catch only when behavior changes


## Type Safety

### Finding
Broad `as` assertions weakened TypeScript safety.

### Why It Matters
Unsafe casts hide DTO/domain mismatch and reduce refactor safety.

### Reject Condition
- broad casting
- `unknown as Xxx`
- bypassing narrowing

### Preferred Pattern
- explicit DTO types
- narrowing
- type guards
- schema validation


## Refactoring Scope

### Finding
Feature PR included unrelated refactoring.

### Why It Matters
Large mixed diffs increase human review cost and regression risk.

### Reject Condition
- unrelated cleanup inside feature PR
- formatting churn mixed with logic changes

### Preferred Pattern
- smallest safe diff
- isolated refactoring PR when necessary


## Design Document Alignment

### Finding
Implementation did not sufficiently follow DESIGN.md intent.

### Why It Matters
Ignoring established project rules causes architectural drift.

### Reject Condition
- implementation contradicts DESIGN.md
- exception policy ignored
- layering constraints bypassed

### Preferred Pattern
- verify relevant DESIGN.md before implementation
- explain intentional deviations
